key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power primarily increases penetration, welding current broadens the weld and stabilizes the arc, and welding speed reduces weld dimensions.
engineering_relevance: Balancing these parameters can support weld geometry and arc stability control when joining low-expansion Invar components for aerospace composite molds.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics
Analysis of laser power, welding speed, and current effects
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, 0.5–0.8 m/min, and 150–170 A, the abstract reports increased penetration with power, reduced penetration and width with speed, and wider welds with more stable arcs at higher current.
watch_item: The reported trends apply to limited parameter ranges; the abstract provides no quantitative simulation–experiment agreement or weld mechanical-property validation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
